title: 10-round AES-256 MITM using the new 6-round distinguisher and early abort

target.description: Ten-round AES-256 with whitening K^0, rounds 1 through 10, and no MixColumns in Round 10, as drawn in Figure 2. The attack uses the standard key schedule and finishes by enumerating the missing four bytes of the preceding round key to recover the complete 256-bit user key.

setting.key_relation: A single unknown AES-256 master key; five key-schedule relations partition the entire key space into 2^64 subspaces that are all searched.
setting.key_population: general secret key; weak-key approach means exhaustive sequential key-space partitioning, not a target weak-key promise
setting.plaintext_model: 2^73 structures of 2^32 chosen plaintexts varying bytes 1,6,11,12, for 2^105 queried blocks in total
assumptions: The authors normalize one 10-round AES encryption as 2^8 table lookups; no independent memory-access calibration is claimed.
The source's final early-abort step tests an initial 192-bit sequence, then extends matches in 16-bit pieces. It retains the precomputed tables of Section 5.2.
All 2^64 key subspaces are included in the total time, while memory is reused between subspaces.
Section 5.2 reports an expected one right pair, but does not give a numerical end-to-end recovery probability for this final Section 5.3 attack.
MixColumns shortcut uses all Fig2 zero-difference conditions, including Delta w7[0,10]=0; a lone guessed Delta z7 byte without those conditions does not determine the remaining bytes.

time.note: Section 5.3 explicitly prices the total as 2^250.5 plus 2^64 times the optimized online expression. No separately rounded optimized-online exponent is given. Preprocessing below is an included component and must not be added again; the 2^253.2 online estimate in Section 5.2 belongs to the unoptimized attack.

data.note: 2^73 structures, each containing 2^32 texts. Section 5.3 changes matching only and retains Section 5.2 data collection.

memory.note: Peak H* storage: at most 2^184 sequences, 16 differences of 16 bits each, i.e. 32 bytes per entry. T5 and T6 are smaller. This native byte count is not a 128-bit-block exponent.

preprocessing.note: Section 5.2 prices Steps 2,3,5 over all 2^64 subspaces; Section 5.3 carries this term unchanged into the total. This is an included component, not extra work beyond reported total time.

success.description: Section5 complete256-bit-key recovery under the source Bernoulli/pair-trial approximation:2^136 pairs with characteristic probability2^-136 give the displayed zero-event complement, about63.2%. This transparently inherits the explicit Section4 success model (PDF10), with Section5's changed pair count and probability; it is not a separately printed Section5 percentage or an empirical AES rate. Steps5–6 enumerate the relevant subspaces, key guesses and all compatible table solutions; Step6(d) exhausts the remaining32 key bits to determine the user key. The model assumes complete branch/table coverage and correct full-key completion/validation, with native source expected table costs. Section5.3 prefix matching retains a correct full match. The existing strict sequence-cardinality/average-branching proof obligation remains; no strict resource cap or actual-AES trial-independence theorem is asserted.

review.scope: Independent source-first and endpoint review verifies this conditional source-model inference, not actual-AES success or a new full-paper audit. The Section4 zero-event law is applied to the Section5 N,p; complete table/branch coverage and full-key verification are explicit model conditions. Native expected costs and the strict support proof obligation remain unchanged.

PDF14 Step5/PDF15 Step6(d):2^184 entries in H* for ONE fixed Theta partition versus a uniformly unrelated256-bit signature. Author average-count model only; the existing branching/support proof obligation remains.
PDF14 Step6(a):32-bit ciphertext-pair filter for the guessed K10, before the input filter.
PDF15 Step6(b): the source about-eight-bit first-round input sieve, reducing expected2^104 pairs to2^96; approximation, not a whole-attack probability.
PDF16 Section5.3: the first192-bit prefix lookup has source ratio2^184/2^192=2^-8 in one H* partition. Conditional remaining16-bit checks are not treated as independent guarantees.

limitations: No attack implementation was executed. The final optimized online phase is specified symbolically by the authors but has no separately rounded exponent; no scalar was invented.
The source claims an improvement against earlier publication-specific data and memory counts, not a current global best-known result.

field_conflicts.label: Conditional sequence cardinality proof
field_conflicts.description: Proposition2 claims at most2^248 sequences, while its state reconstruction invokes Property1, which gives an average solution count, not uniqueness for every difference pair. A strict support bound needs branch multiplicity and filtering aggregation justified. This is a proof obligation, not a demonstrated counterexample to the bound or a substituted attack complexity.
